title: ANOTHER WORLD
subtitle: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).

Anyone who's anyone in the superhero world turns up to San Diego Comic-Con, but with tickets like gold [[1]], many people miss out on the unique experience. items.explainCorrect: Idiom **(like) gold dust** = extremely rare and hard to get — perfect for Comic-Con tickets.

explainIfChosen.0: **Gold powder** is not the fixed idiom for something scarce.
explainIfChosen.3: **Gold flecks** suggests tiny particles — wrong meaning.

items.explainCorrect: **Jump at the chance** = seize an opportunity eagerly.

explainIfChosen.1: **Beam at the chance** is not idiomatic.
explainIfChosen.2: **Plunge at the chance** is not the set phrase.
explainIfChosen.3: **Fly at the chance** is not standard English.

items.explainCorrect: Fixed phrase **beyond your wildest imagination** = more amazing than you could ever imagine.
**The sheer scale** = the enormous size — *sheer* intensifies *scale*.

explainIfChosen.0: **Utter scale** is less natural than *sheer scale*.
explainIfChosen.3: **Wholesale scale** suggests bulk trade — wrong field.

items.explainCorrect: Idiom **go out the window** = be abandoned or forgotten completely.

explainIfChosen.0: **Out the door** can mean leave — not the idiom for plans being discarded.
explainIfChosen.2: **Out the picture** is a different phrase.

items.explainCorrect: **Cut into** (time) = reduce the time available for something else.

explainIfChosen.0: **Creep into** suggests gradual entry — not reducing a schedule.
explainIfChosen.1: **Factor into** means include as a variable — wrong nuance here.
explainIfChosen.3: **Carve into** suggests cutting physically — wrong collocation.

explainIfChosen.0: **Old-school** can describe style — *die-hard* fits devoted fans better.
explainIfChosen.2: **Laid-back** means relaxed — not the usual collocation with *fans* here.

items.explainCorrect: Idiom **only scratch the surface** = barely begin to explore something huge.

explainIfChosen.1: **Pick the surface** is not the idiom.
explainIfChosen.2: **Touch the surface** is possible but *scratch the surface* is the fixed phrase.
